headline: 8 workers killed by toxic gas leak at Sitakunda shipyard
summary: The death toll rose to eight after workers were exposed to poisonous gas while cutting a cylinder at a ship-breaking yard in Chattogram.
details: Eight workers have died following a toxic gas leak at the Ferdous Steel ship-breaking yard in the Station Road area of Bhatiyari Union, Sitakunda, Chattogram.
The incident occurred around 9:00 AM on Friday (August 14) while workers were using machines to cut a gas cylinder from a scrap ship.
Witnesses report that the workers suddenly fell ill due to gas poisoning during the process. Five workers were declared dead upon arrival at the hospital, and three more passed away later.
The deceased have been identified as Sunny Jaldas, Palash Jaldas, Khokon, Rana, Alam, and two brothers, Mansur Ali and Nasir Uddin, along with one other worker.
At least two other workers were injured in the incident and are currently receiving treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital.
Authorities are currently investigating the site to determine the exact cause of the gas leak and the subsequent fatalities.
caption:
8 workers dead in Sitakunda. A routine task of cutting a scrap ship's gas cylinder turned fatal.

Eight workers have died following a toxic gas leak at the Ferdous Steel ship-breaking yard in the Station Road area of Bhatiyari Union, Sitakunda, Chattogram.

The incident occurred around 9:00 AM on Friday (August 14) while workers were using machines to cut a gas cylinder from a scrap ship.

Witnesses report that the workers suddenly fell ill due to gas poisoning during the process. Five workers were declared dead upon arrival at the hospital, and three more passed away later.

The deceased have been identified as Sunny Jaldas, Palash Jaldas, Khokon, Rana, Alam, and two brothers, Mansur Ali and Nasir Uddin, along with one other worker.

At least two other workers were injured in the incident and are currently receiving treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital.

Authorities are currently investigating the site to determine the exact cause of the gas leak and the subsequent fatalities.

headline_marked: Tanzid Hasan [[makes history with first Bangladeshi Test century in Australia]]
headline: Tanzid Hasan makes history with first Bangladeshi Test century in Australia
summary: The opener scored 101 off 188 balls, helping Bangladesh secure a 153-run lead over Australia in the Darwin Test.
details: Bangladesh opener Tanzid Hasan produced a history-making century in only his second Test match, putting his side in a commanding position against Australia in Darwin.
Tanzid became the first Bangladeshi batter to ever score a Test hundred in Australia, scoring a patient 101 runs from 188 balls.
The 25-year-old navigated a formidable pace attack featuring Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, and Josh Hazlewood to reach his maiden Test century.
Tanzid attributed his success to staying calm and playing the ball on its merit, stating he was determined not to overcomplicate his game despite the occasion.
His century came midway through the second session when he pushed Nathan Lyon through mid-off for the single that took him to three figures.
Bangladesh reached 351-6 at stumps on the second day, holding a substantial lead of 153 runs with four wickets remaining.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto praised Tanzid's character and ability to adapt his natural attacking game to the demands of the Test format.
Tanzid's performance served as the cornerstone of Bangladesh's strong response after Australia were dismissed for 198 in their first innings.
caption:
A historic first! Tanzid Hasan becomes the first Bangladeshi to score a Test century in Australia.

Bangladesh opener Tanzid Hasan produced a history-making century in only his second Test match, putting his side in a commanding position against Australia in Darwin.

Tanzid became the first Bangladeshi batter to ever score a Test hundred in Australia, scoring a patient 101 runs from 188 balls.

The 25-year-old navigated a formidable pace attack featuring Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, and Josh Hazlewood to reach his maiden Test century.

Tanzid attributed his success to staying calm and playing the ball on its merit, stating he was determined not to overcomplicate his game despite the occasion.

His century came midway through the second session when he pushed Nathan Lyon through mid-off for the single that took him to three figures.

Bangladesh reached 351-6 at stumps on the second day, holding a substantial lead of 153 runs with four wickets remaining.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto praised Tanzid's character and ability to adapt his natural attacking game to the demands of the Test format.

Tanzid's performance served as the cornerstone of Bangladesh's strong response after Australia were dismissed for 198 in their first innings.
